main_equivalence: The original 4x4 PPT/Schmidt-number-at-least-three target is true if and only if there exist (i) a normalized extreme point rho of the 4x4 PPT-state set, with every real and imaginary entry a real algebraic number, and (ii) a 16x16 Hermitian Gaussian-integer matrix W such that <X|W|X> >= ||X||_F^2 for every complex 4x4 matrix X of rank <=2 and Tr(W rho)<0. In this reduction, r=rank(rho) and s=rank(rho^Gamma) satisfy 2<=r,s<=15 and r^2+s^2<=257, hence min(r,s)<=11. No claim is made that any such pair actually exists.
strict_integer_witness: If a normalized PPT state rho_0 has Schmidt number greater than two, the compact convex normalized Schmidt-number-at-most-two set is strictly separated from it by a Hermitian W_0 that is nonnegative on all rank<=2 projectors and satisfies Tr(W_0 rho_0)<0. Add a sufficiently small positive scalar multiple of I_16: the new W is uniformly positive on normalized rank<=2 vectors and remains negative on rho_0. Approximate its Hermitian entries by Gaussian rationals closely enough to preserve both strict inequalities, then multiply by a sufficiently large positive integer to obtain Gaussian-integer W with rank<=2 margin at least 1 and Tr(W rho_0)<0.
extreme_minimizer: The trace-one PPT set K is compact and convex. Minimize Tr(W rho) over K; its minimum is negative. The minimizers form a nonempty compact face of K and therefore contain an extreme point rho_* of K. Its negative W expectation proves Schmidt number at least three. Thus the target implies the desired extreme state for the same strictly positive integer witness.
extreme_rank_bound: Let P and Q be the support projectors of rho_* and rho_*^Gamma, with ranks r and s. The real Hermitian subspaces {H: PHP=H} and {H: Q H^Gamma Q=H^Gamma} have dimensions r^2 and s^2 in the 256-dimensional real space Herm(16). Their intersection has dimension at least r^2+s^2-256. It contains rho_*. If it contained an independent H, subtract Tr(H)rho_* to obtain a nonzero traceless element H_0 of the intersection; for sufficiently small epsilon, rho_* +/- epsilon H_0 and their partial transposes remain PSD on their fixed supports, contradicting extremality. Hence the intersection has dimension one and r^2+s^2<=257. If r=1 then rho_* is a pure PPT state and hence a product state; if s=1 the same applies to rho_*^Gamma, and partial transpose of a product projector is product. Either would contradict the negative rank-two witness. Thus r,s>=2. If r=16 then the rank inequality forces s<=1, and conversely; hence r,s<=15. Finally r,s>=12 would give r^2+s^2>=288>257, so min(r,s)<=11.
algebraic_state_import: For the fixed Gaussian-integer W, the property that rho belongs to K, Tr(W rho)<0, and rho is extreme in K is a first-order formula over the ordered field of reals with rational coefficients: PSD is expressed by nonnegative principal minors, trace is 1, and extremality says there do not exist distinct sigma,tau in K with 2rho=sigma+tau. This formula has a real solution by the preceding extreme-minimizer argument. By quantifier elimination/transfer for real closed fields, the real algebraic numbers admit a solution as well. The resulting algebraic rho is still extreme and negative, and therefore has the same rank bounds. The real-closed-field theorem is an explicit external mathematical import, not a machine-checked proof.
decidable_in_principle: Independently of the extreme-state refinement, the original target is equivalent to a single first-order sentence over the real numbers: there exist Hermitian 16x16 rho,W such that rho and rho^Gamma are PSD, Tr rho=1, Tr(W rho)<0, and for every complex 4x4 X with ||X||_F^2=1 and all sixteen 3x3 minors zero, <X|W|X> >= 1. The sixteen complex minors give 32 real polynomial equalities; Hermitian PSD is a finite conjunction of nonnegative real principal minors. Necessity is the strict-separation argument and sufficiency is immediate from the witness. Real-closed-field quantifier elimination therefore decides this fixed sentence in principle in either direction. No quantifier-elimination run was performed and no practical complexity or actual yes/no answer is claimed.
